controls.name: bandOn
controls.doc: A band's switch. Off, the band is not in the EQ's bank and its dynamics do not run; on, its static section runs, parked at 0 dB as an EQ band is, and its dynamics run as its dynMode says. A band comes up off, as an EQ band does: the ids and the come-up value are EQ_BAND_ONS's, the EQ's own band switch, and the face holds the two equal at compile time.

controls.name: bandType
controls.doc: The band's shape, in the order of the integer the kernel reads, which is the order of the first three EQ_BAND_TYPES: a bell, a low shelf, a high shelf. A bell's dynamics act through the cookbook bandpass at its centre, a shelf's through half of the first-order allpass at its corner (omx_band_dyn_design).

controls.name: freq
controls.doc: The band's centre or corner, the EQ band's travel by reference. The come-up centres are the EQ's default rule for six bands (omx_eq_default_centres), so the bands start spread across the audio band.

controls.name: gain
controls.doc: The band's static gain, the EQ band's travel by reference: the curve the band draws with its dynamics at rest. 0 dB parks the static section, as on the EQ, and the dynamics still act.

controls.name: q
controls.doc: The bell's Q, the EQ band's travel by reference; the dynamics' bandpass takes the same Q. A shelf reads it as the EQ's shelf does.

controls.name: dynMode
controls.doc: Whether and when the band's dynamics act, in the order of the integer the kernel reads: off, the band is its static section alone; down, it acts above its threshold, when the band is loud (band_dyn's above); up, it acts below its threshold, when the band is quiet (band_dyn's below). The range's sign says whether it cuts or boosts. A band comes up off, so a fresh dynamic EQ is an EQ.

controls.name: threshold
controls.doc: Where the band's dynamics start, in dB of the band's own level after its static section: band_dyn's threshold travel by reference.

controls.name: ratio
controls.doc: How hard the band is held past its threshold: band_dyn's ratio travel by reference.

controls.name: range
controls.doc: The most the dynamics add to the band's static gain, signed: below zero the deepest cut, above zero the largest boost. band_dyn's range travel by reference.

controls.name: attack
controls.doc: The band detector's attack, in ms: band_dyn's attack travel by reference, which stops at the oversampling floor.

controls.name: release
controls.doc: The band detector's release, in ms: band_dyn's release travel by reference.

controls.name: listen
controls.doc: While on, the output is what the band's detector hears, its section B over the signal reaching the band, in place of the EQ's output; with more than one band listening, their sum. It comes up off.

controls.name: mixPct
controls.doc: The share of the processed output, in percent: 100 is the dynamic EQ alone, bit for bit, 0 the input.

readouts.name: band1GainDb
readouts.doc: The gain band 1's dynamics apply now, in dB, both ways: a cut negative, a boost positive, 0 while the band rests, is off or its dynamics are off. The band's gain computer re-run on the level its detector reached at the block's last sample (omx_band_dyn_offset_db), so the reading and the gain the sample took are one computation.

DYNEQ_BANDS.doc: How many bands the dynamic EQ carries, each a static EQ section and its dynamics: six, the floating bands of the reference desks' dynamic EQs. Its state holds this many band-dynamics states.
